## 2

I understand why some images can look suspicious—photos can be edited, and institutions should be questioned. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend only on space photos. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, different stars being visible from different latitudes, Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, time zones, and the way airplanes and satellites operate. These observations come from many independent sources and fit together consistently, whereas a flat-Earth explanation would require many unrelated systems and observations to be misleading at once.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some violet light is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue rather than violet. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more red, orange, and pink light to reach us.

雨下了一整夜，城市像被一层薄纱笼住。路灯在积水里摇晃，映出破碎的金色光斑。屋檐不断滴水，清脆的声音落在寂静中，像有人轻轻敲门。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，轮胎卷起水雾，很快又消失在雨幕里。窗玻璃蒙着朦胧的水汽，我捧着一杯热茶，听雨声填满房间，也听见夜色深处渐渐安静下来的心跳。
